# Sources

<!-- Generated by tools/docs.ts from data/sources.yaml. Do not edit: change the data and run `pnpm docs`. -->

Every source Phosphoros cites, with the date someone last checked that the link works and says what we
cite it for. To add one, open an ["add a source" issue](https://github.com/Xaxis/phosphoros.space/issues/new?template=add-a-source.yml).

## Data

- <a id="nasa-venus-factsheet"></a>Williams, D. R. (NASA Goddard Space Flight Center, NSSDCA) (2024). [Venus Fact Sheet](https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/venusfact.html). Checked 2026-11-20.<br>Mass, radius, orbit, atmosphere mass and composition, surface temperature and pressure, rotation.
- <a id="nasa-earth-factsheet"></a>Williams, D. R. (NASA Goddard Space Flight Center, NSSDCA) (2024). [Earth Fact Sheet](https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/earthfact.html). Checked 2026-11-20.
- <a id="nasa-mercury-factsheet"></a>Williams, D. R. (NASA Goddard Space Flight Center, NSSDCA) (2024). [Mercury Fact Sheet](https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/mercuryfact.html). Checked 2026-11-20.
- <a id="nasa-sun-factsheet"></a>Williams, D. R. (NASA Goddard Space Flight Center, NSSDCA) (2024). [Sun Fact Sheet](https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/sunfact.html). Checked 2026-11-20.
- <a id="nist-co2"></a>National Institute of Standards and Technology. [NIST Chemistry WebBook, SRD 69: Carbon dioxide, phase change data](https://webbook.nist.gov/cgi/cbook.cgi?ID=C124389&Mask=4). Checked 2026-11-20.<br>Triple point 216.58 K and 5.185 bar, critical point 304.13 K and 73.77 bar, sublimation enthalpy.
- <a id="jpl-sbdb-ceres"></a>NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory, Solar System Dynamics. [JPL Small-Body Database: 1 Ceres](https://ssd.jpl.nasa.gov/tools/sbdb_lookup.html#/?sstr=1). Checked 2026-11-20.<br>Ceres's semi-major axis and aphelion.

## Papers and books

- <a id="iau-2015-nominal"></a>Mamajek, E. E., Prsa, A., Torres, G., et al. (2015). [IAU 2015 Resolution B3 on Recommended Nominal Conversion Constants for Selected Solar and Planetary Properties](https://arxiv.org/abs/1510.07674). Checked 2026-11-20.<br>Nominal solar radius and luminosity.
- <a id="kopp-lean-2011"></a>Kopp, G., and Lean, J. L. (2011). [A new, lower value of total solar irradiance: Evidence and climate significance](https://doi.org/10.1029/2010GL045777). Geophysical Research Letters 38, L01706. Checked 2026-11-20.<br>The solar constant at Earth, 1,361 W/m².
- <a id="codata-2018"></a>Tiesinga, E., Mohr, P. J., Newell, D. B., and Taylor, B. N. (2021). [CODATA recommended values of the fundamental physical constants: 2018](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.93.025010). Reviews of Modern Physics 93, 025010. [Free copy](https://physics.nist.gov/cuu/Constants/archive2018.html). Checked 2026-11-20.<br>The 2022 adjustment leaves every constant we use unchanged at the precision we use.
- <a id="park-2016-ceres"></a>Park, R. S., Konopliv, A. S., Bills, B. G., et al. (2016). [A partially differentiated interior for (1) Ceres deduced from its gravity field and shape](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature18955). Nature 537, 515 to 517. Checked 2026-11-20.<br>Ceres's mass and mean radius from Dawn.
- <a id="ceres-water"></a>McCord, T. B., and Sotin, C. (2005). [Ceres: Evolution and current state](https://doi.org/10.1029/2004JE002244). Journal of Geophysical Research: Planets 110, E05009. Checked 2026-11-20.<br>Ceres's density suggests 17 to 27% water by mass. This estimate predates the Dawn mission; the model's 27% is the top of that range and the program's "40% of Ceres's water" depends on it. Post-Dawn interior models (Ermakov et al. 2017, doi:10.1002/2017JE005302) are the next source to check.
- <a id="basalt-thermal"></a>Robertson, E. C. (1988). [Thermal properties of rocks](https://doi.org/10.3133/ofr88441). U.S. Geological Survey Open-File Report 88-441. Checked 2026-11-20.<br>Dense basalt conducts about 2.0 W/(m·K) by extrapolated measurement and 2.55 W/(m·K) calculated from its minerals. The model uses 2.5, the upper value, which slightly overstates crust heat flow.
- <a id="smrekar-2023-heatflow"></a>Smrekar, S. E., Ostberg, C., and O'Rourke, J. G. (2023). [Earth-like lithospheric thickness and heat flow on Venus consistent with active rifting](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41561-022-01068-0). Nature Geoscience 16, 13 to 18. Checked 2026-11-20.
- <a id="ei-statistical-review"></a>Energy Institute (2025). [Statistical Review of World Energy 2025](https://www.energyinst.org/statistical-review). Checked 2026-11-20.<br>Global primary energy of about 590 EJ in 2024, an average of 1.9 × 10¹³ W.
- <a id="sagan-1961"></a>Sagan, C. (1961). [The Planet Venus](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.133.3456.849). Science 133, 849 to 858. Checked 2026-11-20.
- <a id="adelman-1982"></a>Adelman, S. J. (1982). [Can Venus be transformed into an Earth-like planet?](https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/1982JBIS...35....3A/abstract). Journal of the British Interplanetary Society 35, 3. Checked 2026-11-20.<br>End page not confirmed; no DOI exists.
- <a id="birch-1991"></a>Birch, P. (1991). [Terraforming Venus Quickly](https://www.orionsarm.com/fm_store/TerraformingVenusQuickly.pdf). Journal of the British Interplanetary Society 44, 157 to 167. Checked 2026-11-20.<br>The author's own site no longer resolves; an archived copy is at https://web.archive.org/web/20201204191839/http://www.paulbirch.net/TerraformingVenusQuickly.pdf
- <a id="bullock-grinspoon-1996"></a>Bullock, M. A., and Grinspoon, D. H. (1996). [The stability of climate on Venus](https://doi.org/10.1029/95JE03862). Journal of Geophysical Research: Planets 101, 7521 to 7529. Checked 2026-11-20.
- <a id="landis-2003"></a>Landis, G. A. (2003). [Colonization of Venus](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.1541418). AIP Conference Proceedings 654, 1193 to 1198. Checked 2026-11-20.
- <a id="landis-2011"></a>Landis, G. A. (2011). [Terraforming Venus: A Challenging Project for Future Colonization](https://doi.org/10.2514/6.2011-7215). AIAA SPACE 2011 Conference and Exposition, AIAA 2011-7215. Checked 2026-11-20.
- <a id="havoc-2015"></a>Arney, D. C., and Jones, C. A. (2015). [High Altitude Venus Operational Concept (HAVOC): An Exploration Strategy for Venus](https://doi.org/10.2514/6.2015-4612). AIAA SPACE 2015, AIAA 2015-4612. [Free copy](https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/20160006329). Checked 2026-11-20.
- <a id="howe-2022"></a>Howe, A. R. (2022). [Cloud Continents: Terraforming Venus Efficiently by Means of a Floating Artificial Surface](https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.06722). Journal of the British Interplanetary Society 75, 42 to 47. Checked 2026-11-20.
- <a id="nasa-mars-magnetic-2017"></a>Green, J. L., Hollingsworth, J., Brain, D., et al. (2017). [A Future Mars Environment for Science and Exploration](https://www.hou.usra.edu/meetings/V2050/pdf/8250.pdf). Planetary Science Vision 2050 Workshop, LPI Contribution 1989, abstract 8250. Checked 2026-11-20.<br>A magnetic dipole at Mars L1 to shield the planet from the solar wind; the model for Aegis.
- <a id="angel-2006"></a>Angel, R. (2006). [Feasibility of cooling the Earth with a cloud of small spacecraft near the inner Lagrange point (L1)](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.0608163103). PNAS 103, 17184 to 17189. Checked 2026-11-20.<br>A shade of thin refracting flyers that bend sunlight a few degrees rather than reflect it, so light pressure barely moves them, holding station near L1. The model for the version 3 Veil.
- <a id="forward-1991"></a>Forward, R. L. (1991). [Statite: A spacecraft that does not orbit](https://doi.org/10.2514/3.26287). Journal of Spacecraft and Rockets 28, 606 to 611. Checked 2026-11-20.<br>A statite hovers where light pressure pushes it away from the body whose gravity pulls it.
- <a id="sanchez-mcinnes-2015"></a>Sanchez, J.-P., and McInnes, C. R. (2015). [Optimal Sunshade Configurations for Space-Based Geoengineering near the Sun-Earth L1 Point](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0136648). PLOS ONE 10, e0136648. Checked 2026-11-20.<br>Light pressure moves a sunshade's equilibrium sunward of L1.
- <a id="nasa-cp-2255"></a>Freitas, R. A., Jr., and Gilbreath, W. P. (eds.) (1982). [Advanced Automation for Space Missions, Chapter 5: Replicating Systems Concepts: Self-Replicating Lunar Factory and Demonstration](https://nss.org/wp-content/uploads/2017/07/1982-Self-Replicating-Lunar-Factory.pdf). NASA Conference Publication 2255 (1980 NASA/ASEE Summer Study), pp. 189 to 335. Checked 2026-11-20.<br>A 100 t seed factory on the Moon that copies itself in about a year.
- <a id="jensen-2024"></a>Jensen, D. W. (2024). [Design Limits on Large Space Stations](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.00152). Checked 2026-11-20.<br>Summarizes the 1980 lunar factory in one paragraph (section 4.1); cite CP-2255 for detail.
- <a id="santhanam-2012"></a>Santhanam, P., Gray, D. J., and Ram, R. J. (2012). [Thermoelectrically Pumped Light-Emitting Diodes Operating above Unity Efficiency](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.108.097403). Physical Review Letters 108, 097403. Checked 2026-11-20.<br>An LED that emits 69 pW of light from 30 pW of electricity, drawing the rest from heat.
- <a id="casado-2019"></a>Casado, A., Radevici, I., Sadi, T., and Oksanen, J. (2019). [Temperature dependence of thermophotonic energy transfer in intracavity structures](https://doi.org/10.1117/12.2506227). Proc. SPIE 10936, Photonic Heat Engines: Science and Applications, 109360U. [Free copy](https://acris.aalto.fi/ws/portalfiles/portal/38407803/109360U.pdf). Checked 2026-11-20.
- <a id="licht-2025-c2cnt"></a>Licht, G., Hofstetter, K., and Licht, S. (2025). [Large-scale electrolytic molten carbonate carbon capture and transformation to carbon nanotubes and other graphene nanocarbons](https://doi.org/10.1017/cat.2025.10007). Cambridge Prisms: Carbon Technologies 1, e6. Checked 2026-11-20.<br>The C2CNT process splits CO₂ dissolved in molten carbonate into graphene nanocarbons and oxygen in one step.
- <a id="licht-2015"></a>Licht, S. (2015). [Carbon nanofibers, precious commodities from sunlight & CO2 to ameliorate global warming](https://arxiv.org/abs/1503.06727). Checked 2026-11-20.<br>Notes that sulfur gases are reduced to sulfur in the electrolysis chamber and do not poison it, citing Kaplan, Wachtel and Lubomirsky (2013). The paper does not use the name C2CNT.
- <a id="ren-2015"></a>Ren, J., Li, F.-F., Lau, J., Gonzalez-Urbina, L., and Licht, S. (2015). [One-Pot Synthesis of Carbon Nanofibers from CO2](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.nanolett.5b02427). Nano Letters 15, 6142 to 6148. Checked 2026-11-20.
- <a id="kaplan-2013"></a>Kaplan, V., Wachtel, E., and Lubomirsky, I. (2013). [Carbonate melt regeneration for efficient capture of SO2 from coal combustion](https://doi.org/10.1039/c3ra42654h). RSC Advances 3, 15842. Checked 2026-11-20.
- <a id="rocketlab-2026-neutron"></a>Rocket Lab USA (2026). [Rocket Lab Form 8-K, exhibit 99.1 (Neutron first launch moved to 2027)](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001819994/000181999426000067/rklb-10142026ex991.htm). Checked 2026-11-20.

## Law and policy

- <a id="iau-2012-au"></a>International Astronomical Union (2012). [IAU 2012 Resolution B2: re-definition of the astronomical unit of length](https://www.iau.org/administration/resolutions/general_assemblies/). Checked 2026-11-20.<br>The astronomical unit is exactly 149,597,870,700 m.
- <a id="outer-space-treaty"></a>United Nations Office for Outer Space Affairs (1967). [Treaty on Principles Governing the Activities of States in the Exploration and Use of Outer Space, including the Moon and Other Celestial Bodies](https://www.unoosa.org/unoosa/en/ourwork/spacelaw/treaties/outerspacetreaty.html). Checked 2026-11-20.<br>Article II bars national appropriation; Article IX requires avoiding harmful contamination.
- <a id="cospar-pp"></a>Committee on Space Research. [COSPAR Policy on Planetary Protection](https://cosparhq.cnes.fr/cospar-policy-on-planetary-protection/). Checked 2026-11-20.
